browser.name: Firefox
browser.userAgent: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64; rv:158.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/158.0

tests.name: Page is a secure context (WebCrypto and the camera need this)
tests.detail: yes (http://localhost:8080)

tests.name: This page cannot send anything over the network
tests.detail: a test request was blocked by the page's own security policy before leaving the browser

tests.name: WebCrypto exists; SHA-256 and random numbers work
tests.detail: SHA-256 test value matches

tests.name: Ed25519: create a key pair whose private key is marked non-extractable
tests.detail: key pair created; private key says extractable = false

tests.name: Ed25519: the private key really cannot be exported; the public key can
tests.detail: every export attempt on the private key was refused; public key exported as 32 bytes

tests.name: Ed25519: sign, verify, and reject a changed message and a wrong key
tests.detail: 64-byte signature; good=true, changed message=false, wrong key=false

tests.name: Ed25519: the same message always gives the same signature (RFC 8032)
tests.detail: two signatures were identical

tests.name: Ed25519: matches the official RFC 8032 test vectors exactly
tests.detail: TEST 1 (empty message): signature identical, official signature verifies; TEST 2 (one byte): signature identical, official signature verifies

tests.name: Fallback: ECDSA P-256 sign and verify with a non-extractable key
tests.detail: works; signature is 64 bytes in raw r||s form (the server would need to convert it if it expects DER)

tests.name: Ed25519 key stays non-extractable after being stored and reloaded
tests.detail: stored, reloaded, still non-extractable, and still signs correctly

tests.name: ECDSA P-256 key stays non-extractable after being stored and reloaded
tests.detail: stored, reloaded, still non-extractable, and still signs correctly

tests.name: Browser storage: can the page ask the browser not to delete its data?
tests.detail: persist() exists; already persistent: false; quota about 10240 MB. NOT TESTED HERE: some browsers (notably Safari) delete a site's data after about 7 days without a visit. The SDK must re-register a key if it is gone.

tests.name: MediaStreamTrackProcessor: read raw video frames straight from a video track
tests.detail: not present in this browser

tests.name: VideoFrame: the raw-frame object used by WebCodecs
tests.detail: present

tests.name: VideoDecoder: WebCodecs decoder (to read the picture inside encoded frames)
tests.detail: present

tests.name: OffscreenCanvas: draw and read pixels inside a worker
tests.detail: present

tests.name: createImageBitmap: turn a frame into a transferable image
tests.detail: present

tests.name: requestVideoFrameCallback: be told exactly when a new video frame is ready
tests.detail: present

tests.name: ImageCapture: grab a single frame from a camera track
tests.detail: not present in this browser

tests.name: RTCRtpScriptTransform: standard Insertable Streams (encoded frames, in a worker)
tests.detail: present

tests.name: RTCRtpReceiver.createEncodedStreams: older Chrome-style Insertable Streams
tests.detail: not present in this browser

tests.group: 4b. Frame access: reading a local video (made on a canvas, no camera)
tests.name: Read frames as pixels via a video element and canvas (works everywhere)
tests.detail: 10 frames at 320x240 in 1.26s, and the pixels changed between frames (live video)

tests.group: 4b. Frame access: reading a local video (made on a canvas, no camera)
tests.name: Read raw VideoFrame objects with MediaStreamTrackProcessor
tests.detail: MediaStreamTrackProcessor does not exist here; the SDK would use the video-element path instead

tests.group: 4b. Frame access: reading a local video (made on a canvas, no camera)
tests.name: Grab single frames with ImageCapture.grabFrame()
tests.detail: ImageCapture does not exist here

tests.group: 4c. Frame access: inside a worker (the SDK reads frames off the main thread)
tests.name: Send a frame to a worker as an image and read its pixels there
tests.detail: worker read a 320x240 frame and its pixels

tests.group: 4c. Frame access: inside a worker (the SDK reads frames off the main thread)
tests.name: Hand a VideoFrame to a worker (transfer, not copy)
tests.detail: worker received a 320x240 VideoFrame and turned it into an image

tests.group: 4c. Frame access: inside a worker (the SDK reads frames off the main thread)
tests.name: Does MediaStreamTrackProcessor exist INSIDE a worker? (some browsers offer it only there)
tests.detail: inside a worker: MediaStreamTrackProcessor no, MediaStreamTrackGenerator no, VideoFrame yes, OffscreenCanvas yes

tests.group: 4c. Frame access: inside a worker (the SDK reads frames off the main thread)
tests.name: Hand the whole video track to a worker and read frames there
tests.detail: a worker here has no MediaStreamTrackProcessor, so a track could not be read there even if it could be sent

tests.group: 4d. Frame access: decoding (needed to look inside encoded frames)
tests.name: WebCodecs: which video codecs can be decoded
tests.detail: VP8: yes, VP9: yes, H.264: yes, AV1: yes

tests.group: 4e. Frame access: a call (receiver-side scoring, decision D-02)
tests.name: Make a loopback call inside the page and read the encoded frames passing through
tests.detail: call connected. Using RTCRtpScriptTransform (standard, runs in a worker): 32 frames seen leaving the sender, 40 frames arriving at the receiver in about 3 seconds

tests.group: 4e. Frame access: a call (receiver-side scoring, decision D-02)
tests.name: Read the RECEIVED video as pixels (video element and canvas)
tests.detail: 10 received frames at 320x240 in 0.98s; the pixels changed (live)

tests.group: 4e. Frame access: a call (receiver-side scoring, decision D-02)
tests.name: Read the RECEIVED video as raw VideoFrame objects
tests.detail: MediaStreamTrackProcessor does not exist here; receiver-side scoring would use the video-element path

tests.group: 5. Platform (for the on-device model, step P0-21)
tests.name: WebAssembly, and its SIMD speed-up
tests.detail: WebAssembly present; SIMD supported

tests.group: 5. Platform (for the on-device model, step P0-21)
tests.name: Multi-threaded WebAssembly (needs a cross-origin-isolated page)
tests.detail: cross-origin isolated: false; SharedArrayBuffer: false; CPU cores reported: 8. This test page is not isolated on purpose, so 'false' is expected here. It only shows the browser could do it if a partner's page sends the right headers.

tests.group: 5. Platform (for the on-device model, step P0-21)
tests.name: Graphics acceleration: WebGPU and WebGL2
tests.detail: WebGPU: available; WebGL2: available
